title: Polylogarithmic updates for bounded rank-width
formal: Can a rank-decomposition of width at most C(k+1) be maintained in f(k) log^c(n+2) amortized update time under the promise that rank-width never exceeds k?
definitions: Use a uniform word-RAM with words of Θ(log(n+2)) bits, unit-cost word arithmetic, Boolean operations, shifts, comparisons and memory accesses, and no nonuniform advice. Constants may be enlarged to address the stated space. The vertex set [n] is fixed, graphs are simple and undirected, and updates insert an absent edge or delete a present edge. Unless stated otherwise the graph starts empty; all outputs must be correct for every legal update sequence. A rank-decomposition for n≥2 is a tree of maximum degree three whose leaves correspond bijectively to graph vertices. Each tree edge splits the leaves into A and V\A. Its cut rank is the rank over F_2 of the adjacency submatrix with rows A and columns V\A. Width is the maximum cut rank, and rank-width is the minimum width over all such trees. For n≤1 define width zero. The parameter k≥0 is supplied. Seek a deterministic structure, an absolute constant C, an absolute exponent c and a computable function f, all independent of n and sequence length. It must initialize in f(k)n^{O(1)} time, use f(k)n² log^c(n+2) words, and maintain an implicit decomposition after each update. An extraction query must output its tree and leaf labels in f(k)n log^c(n+2) time without changing the update guarantee. For U updates and Q extractions total time excluding initialization is at most f(k)(U+Qn)log^c(n+2). There is no promise-violation detection requirement; outside the rank-width promise no guarantee is demanded. This extraction interface avoids charging linear output after every update.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked algorithm and proof of the specified correctness and resource guarantees, or prove that this precise target is impossible. Any conditional impossibility must explicitly state its hypothesis and the implication proved.
context: The dynamic rank-width result has subpolynomial update dependence on n. This target asks to replace that factor by a fixed polylogarithm.
why: This asks whether a structural graph parameter supports genuinely polylogarithmic dynamic maintenance.
